title: Overlay stitch square
subtitle: Colour patterns applied over a solid base fabric using front-post spike stitches
excerpt: The overlay square crochets a plain dc grid first, then works front-post stitches in a contrast colour across the surface on a second pass — the overlay layer sits on top of the base without structurally changing it. Geometric diamond and stripe patterns emerge from the overlay without any colour-change complexity in the base.
sourceNotes: Overlay crochet techniques appear in Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 5 (1890), decorative surface chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: An overlay stitch crochet square in cream base with a deep teal diamond overlay pattern on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Diamond outline visible across the dc base, 11 cm square.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished square measures 11 × 11 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Overlay stitch square
chartDefinition.caption: Base layer: dc rows in colour A. Overlay layer: front-post spike stitches in colour B applied across the surface. Diamond pattern shown.

glossaryTerms.definition: A front-post or spike stitch worked in a contrast colour across the surface of a completed base fabric. The overlay stitches sit on top of the base without being structurally load-bearing.

content.text: separates construction from decoration: work the base square in dc first, then apply the pattern as a second pass in a contrast colour. No colour changes during the base rows; no complex counting while adding the pattern.

The front-post trebles of the overlay reach down one or two rows into the base fabric, sitting proud of the surface. A diamond outline uses four overlay stitches placed at the corners of a tilted square; a stripe uses a row of overlay stitches across the full width every three rows.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 10 g colour A (base) and 4 g colour B (overlay) in DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Ch 16. Row 1: dc in 2nd ch from hook, dc to end. (15 dc.) Turn. Work rows 2–10 in dc, ch 1 each row. Fasten off. (10-row, 15-stitch base square.)

Join colour B at the bottom right corner. Work a fptr reaching 2 rows down at the positions that form the diamond outline. On row 5 (the widest point), work fptr at position 1 and position 15. On rows 4 and 6, work at positions 3 and 13. On rows 3 and 7, at positions 5 and 11. On rows 2 and 8, at positions 7 and 9. On row 1 (bottom), a single fptr at position 8 closes the diamond.
For a fully integrated two-colour pattern, try the tapestry crochet square, where both colours are worked simultaneously into each row.
